sources.entry: 📖 The Pragmatic Programmer: From Journeyman to Master: hands-on the most inspiring and useful book I've read about programming.

summary.title: The Pragmatic Programmer, 20th Anniversary Edition
summary.one_liner: A classic, language-independent guide to software development practices, covering craftsmanship, design, tooling, testing, concurrency, and career habits.
takeaways: Practical, language-independent principles for writing maintainable, flexible software
Techniques such as DRY, orthogonality, tracer bullets, and design by contract
Habits for testing (including property-based testing), debugging, and version control
Approaches to requirements, teamwork, concurrency, and career responsibility
summary.summary: This is the 20th Anniversary Edition of Andy Hunt and Dave Thomas's classic book on software development, published in 2019 (320 pages, ISBN 9780135957059). The page describes it as a series of self-contained, short topic sections with anecdotes, analogies, and exercises, aimed at new coders, experienced programmers, and managers. Topics listed include personal responsibility, architecture for adaptable code, basic tools, testing, concurrency, requirements, teams, and the Pragmatic Starter Kit. The page also lists release notes and ebook formats (PDF, epub, mobi) and print purchase options, which are mostly sales information.
